Te tumbas en un túnel ruidoso, sin rayos: You lie down in a noisy tunnel, with no X-rays or ionising radiation, and a detailed image of your knee or your brain comes out. Behind it there is a giant magnet, radio waves and the frequency at which the protons of your water spin.

<b>1938</b>Isidor Rabi mide la resonanci: 1938Isidor Rabi measures the magnetic resonance of nuclei in a beam of molecules: it is the first nuclear magnetic resonance experiment. He receives the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1944.
<b>1946</b>Felix Bloch y Edward Purcell,: 1946Felix Bloch and Edward Purcell, separately, detect resonance in liquids and solids. They share the 1952 Nobel Prize in Physics.
<b>1973</b>Paul Lauterbur propone usar g: 1973Paul Lauterbur proposes using field gradients to locate the signal and obtains the first image; Peter Mansfield improves the technique. Both receive the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2003.
<b>1977</b>Raymond Damadian y su equipo: 1977Raymond Damadian and his team obtain the first image of an entire human body, after many hours of scanning.
<b>Desde 1980</b>Los equipos clínicos se: Since 1980Clinical scanners spread through hospitals: today 1.5 and 3 T ones are common, and there are 7 T ones for research.
El imán del escáner es un solenoide enor: The scanner's magnet is an enormous solenoid: its field at the centre is given by Ampère's law, and from it comes the frequency at which the radio pulse has to be emitted.

es el campo del imán de un equipo habitu: is the magnet field of a typical scanner: about 30,000 times that of the Earth, which is around 50 µT.
El túnel del escáner es en realidad un <: The scanner's tunnel is actually a solenoid: thousands of turns of superconducting wire, cooled to almost −269 °C, carrying hundreds of amperes without using energy. Inside it creates a very intense and uniform field, $B_0 = μ_0 n I$.\n\nThat field, always on and always in the same direction, is not the image: it is just the stage. It needs to be almost identical throughout the patient's volume, because the signal that is measured will depend on its value, point by point.
es la frecuencia de giro de un protón en: is the spin frequency of a proton in the field: about 63.9 MHz at 1.5 T (42.58 MHz per tesla).
El cuerpo es sobre todo agua, y cada mol: The body is mostly water, and each water molecule has two hydrogen nuclei: two protons. A proton behaves like a tiny magnet that also spins on itself (it has spin).\n\nIn a field $B_0$ that tiny magnet does not simply line up: it precesses, like a tilted spinning top turning around the vertical, at the Larmor frequency $f = (γ/2π) B_0$. The frequency only depends on the field: if $B_0$ changes a little, its frequency changes. With the slider you can see other scanners.
es el exceso de protones alineados a fav: is the excess of protons aligned with the field at 1.5 T and 37 °C; all the signal comes from that small surplus.
Casi todos los protones se compensan uno: Almost all the protons cancel each other out; only a tiny excess aligned with the field remains, about 5 in every million. But there are so many that they add up to a measurable magnetisation, $M$, parallel to $B_0$.\n\nTo move it, a radio pulse is emitted exactly at the Larmor frequency, 63.9 MHz. This is resonance: only if the frequency matches does the pulse push the protons, which tilt up to 90° and start to rotate all together and in phase. At any other frequency, nothing moves.
es la tensión que aparece en la bobina r: is the voltage that appears in the receiver coil because the magnetisation rotates and its flux changes.
Al acabar el pulso, la magnetización inc: When the pulse ends, the tilted magnetisation keeps rotating at 63.9 MHz. It is a magnet spinning near a coil: by Faraday's law it induces an alternating voltage in it, and that voltage is the radio signal that gets amplified.\n\nThe signal does not last: the protons return to equilibrium with two times, $T_1$ (they recover their alignment with the field) and $T_2$ (they lose phase with each other). Each tissue has its own: fat recovers in a fraction of a second and cerebrospinal fluid takes several seconds. That difference is what gives contrast to the image. The values in the graph are approximate at 1.5 T.
es lo que cambia la frecuencia por cada: is how much the frequency changes per centimetre with a gradient of 10 mT/m.
Hasta aquí sabemos que hay señal, pero n: So far we know there is a signal, but not where it comes from. The trick: extra coils, the gradients, make the field grow linearly with position, $B(x) = B_0 + G x$.\n\nSince the frequency depends on the field, each slice of the body precesses at its own frequency: $f(x) = (γ/2π)(B_0 + G x)$. With $G = 10 "mT/m"$, at 20 cm from the centre the frequency changes by $±85 "kHz"$. By measuring which frequencies arrive and with what intensity, a computer reconstructs the map of the body (a Fourier transform). Move the slider to see the effect of a larger gradient.

es la frecuencia de Larmor del protón en: is the Larmor frequency of the proton at the centre of the 1.5 T magnet.
Con un solenoide de 2 m con 4775 espiras: With a 2 m solenoid with 4775 turns ($n = 2387.5 "turns/m"$) and 500 A, the field at the centre is $B_0 = μ_0 n I = 4π·10^{−7} · 2387.5 · 500 ≈ 1.500 "T"$.\n\nThe Larmor frequency is $f = 42.577 "MHz/T" · 1.500 "T" ≈ 63.87 "MHz"$ (at 3 T it would be 127.7 MHz). The magnetostatics tool calculates that field with Biot-Savart and Ampère for any solenoid. The data are indicative: a real magnet is made with several coils and its field is very uniform in a sphere of about 40 cm.
